The interface's controls now come from GlimStone itself rather than being rebuilt from its description, and the last control that still came from the operating system is gone. The engine is unchanged.

## 🎨 Design

- **The controls are the design language's own files now, not this app's reading of them.** GlimStone 1.7.0 started shipping its button, switch, card, badge, dropdown, dialog, toast, info bubble and about card as source, for the reason this app kept running into: two programs built from one document end up speaking the same language in two dialects, and every rule after that has to be applied twice by hand. They are copied here and edited nowhere. Where a copy needed to behave differently, the property was added to the language and the file was copied again.
- **The borrowed stylesheet block is gone.** The components arrived needing thirteen classes and seven measurements that only existed inside BombVault, so this app carried a copy of somebody else's rules and marked it as a loan. GlimStone 1.7.1 defines them itself and the loan went back.
- **Every picker in the app is one control.** The language, the storage kind, the drive and the path picker were four native `<select>` elements; they are now the same portalled, edge-aware listbox, opening upward when there is no room below.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The languages have real flags.** The list showed a small `DE` where a flag belongs. Windows draws the flag emoji's two codepoints as a two-letter tag rather than a flag, which is Microsoft's own long-standing policy in its emoji font and true of every program on the machine, so it could not be fixed while the list was a native one: an `<option>` can hold nothing but text. Now that the list is drawn by the page, each entry carries the same flag artwork the other programs here use. Catalan, Galician and Basque get theirs for the first time, because there is no emoji for a subdivision at all.
- **The autostart switch is checked on the wire.** It worked, and nothing tested it: the test read the answer into a shape that does not carry those two fields, so it walked past them, and the switch could have been renamed or dropped without a single test noticing.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The About card names the design language version it is actually built from**, and that is now a published release rather than a tag without one.
- **A picker no longer grows with the name inside it.** Forty-two language names go through the same control, and the longest of them used to decide how wide the field was.
